content: Patients treated with neomycin should be under close clinical observation due to the potential for significant toxicity associated with its use. Neurotoxicity, including ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity, has been reported even when neomycin is used at recommended doses. The risk of these adverse effects is higher in patients with impaired renal function. Nephrotoxicity and permanent bilateral auditory and vestibular ototoxicity can occur in patients with preexisting renal damage and even in those with normal renal function, particularly when treated with higher doses or for longer durations than recommended. High-frequency hearing loss is often the first sign of ototoxicity and may only be detected through audiometric testing. Serial vestibular and audiometric tests, as well as renal function assessments, should be performed, especially in high-risk patients. Ototoxicity is often delayed in onset, and patients developing cochlear damage may not exhibit symptoms during therapy to warn them of impending eighth nerve destruction. Total or partial deafness may occur long after neomycin has been discontinued. Neomycin can also cause neuromuscular blockade, which may result in respiratory depression or paralysis. This risk is heightened in patients receiving concurrent neuromuscular blocking agents or those with underlying neuromuscular disorders.
